title: Why an explainer is a JSON outline, not a page you write
subtitle: The idea behind make-explainer, what it guarantees, and where it stops

sections.title: An outline, not a page, keeps explainers consistent
sections.label: The verdict
sections.text: You write the facts; the tool owns the layout. The page is always well formed, offline and the same family as every other one.
points: The model fills typed sections in JSON and never writes HTML, CSS or script.
Checks run before the build: schema, file references, prose rules.
One theme, one accent and one set of components keep every page consistent.

sections.title: A hand-written page drifts, a generated one cannot
sections.label: The problem
sections.text:
A page written freehand looks fine once. The second one uses a different spacing scale, the third a different set of colours, and the fourth quietly pulls a font from a CDN.

With an outline, the layout is not up for discussion. Each section **type** has one renderer, and the renderer is the only place that knows about markup. The `title` of a section is a claim a reader can agree or disagree with, not a label such as "Overview".

Text fields accept a small subset of markdown: bold, italic, `code`, [links to https pages](https://example.com) and `- ` lists. Anything else is shown as plain text, so a stray angle bracket can never become a tag.

sections.title: Three steps from facts to a finished page
sections.label: The pipeline
sections.alt: Three boxes joined by arrows, top to bottom: Outline, Checks, Page.
sections.caption: The outline is typed JSON sections, the checks cover schema, links and prose, and the page is one offline HTML file. A bad outline never reaches the build.

sections.title: Four rules keep the output trustworthy
sections.label: Guarantees

items.title: Closed vocabulary
items.text: Tones, severities and changes come from fixed lists. A typo gets a did-you-mean hint instead of a silent default.

items.title: Files stay local
items.text: Images and diagrams resolve inside the spec folder. Absolute paths, parent folders and symlinks are refused.

items.title: Plain prose
items.text: A lint rejects emoji, filler phrases and placeholder text before the page exists.

items.title: Status needs a word
items.text: Severity, change type and step status each show a shape and a label, never colour alone.

sections.verdict: Use the outline for recaps, checklists and concept pages. Reach for a bespoke page only when the layout itself is the point.

sections.title: Three limits you should know about
sections.label: Limits

items.risk: A layout the section types cannot express
items.mitigation: Split the content across sections, or build a bespoke page for that one case.

items.risk: A diagram or chart needs a sibling skill
items.mitigation: The installer adds make-diagram and make-dashboard next to this skill.

items.risk: A very large inline image bloats the page
items.mitigation: Images over 1.5 MB are rejected; resize or link a smaller export.

sections.title: Text is escaped, not trusted
sections.text: A field such as `` is shown as characters on the page. If you need real markup, the section type is missing, not the escape.

sections.summary: Why not let the model write HTML directly?
sections.text:
It can, but then every page needs its own review for network calls, broken markup and style drift.

- The outline removes that review.
- It also makes pages diffable: a change is a change to JSON.
